content: Slack ingestion observes from the existing interactive bot's identity (its token, its channel membership) rather than a separate read-only observer app; write-safety is enforced at the collector's code path (no write call sites, an API client allowlisted to the read families, dependency-ceiling script) since credential-level read-only enforcement is unavailable for a single app identity. The interactive bot and collector share one workspace rate budget; steady-state observation is watermark polling with socket-mode events as a later freshness optimization only.
rationale: The requirement is bot-perspective indexing: the bot's channel membership defines what it indexes so it can search its own history when directed by humans, and the ratified connector identity model already binds the minted Slack scope to the observer bot identity. A Slack app carries one bot token per install with all granted scopes, so no read-only credential exists for the same identity. Operator ruled 2026-08-13; first consumer is an existing operator bot with vault-resolved credentials via the op CLI.
